headline: Saudi Industry Forum opens in Jeddah under Makkah governor's patronage
deck: The Jeddah forum carries the Makkah governor's patronage and a ministry partnership across nine industrial themes, but four days out its agenda is unpublished.
excerpt: The Saudi Industry Forum opens at Jeddah Superdome on 14 September under the patronage of the Governor of Makkah Region, with organiser targets of 150 exhibitors and 80 speakers.
content:
The Saudi Industry Forum opens at the Jeddah Superdome on 14 September, running to 16 September under the patronage of Prince Khalid Al-Faisal bin Abdulaziz, Governor of Makkah Region. It is organised by the Federation of Saudi Chambers through its National Industrial Committee with the Jeddah Chamber, in strategic partnership with the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources, under the theme Innovation for Sustainability.

The programme is structured around nine axes: food and pharmaceutical industries; automotive; perfumes and cosmetics; entrepreneurship and innovation; logistics; renewable energy; industrial sustainability; innovative manufacturing technologies; and advanced transformation industries. Arabic coverage adds knowledge localisation, the fourth industrial revolution, artificial intelligence and automation among the discussion topics.

The organiser's targets are 150 or more exhibitors, more than 80 speakers, over 15,000 visitors and more than 50 sessions. Those are projections, and the useful check on them is the forum's first edition, held at Dhahran Expo in June 2025, which delivered 320-plus exhibitors and 78 speakers. On that evidence the machinery to run an event of this size exists, and the 2026 targets are conservative rather than ambitious.

The 2025 edition also produced concrete outputs, which is the more relevant precedent for what to expect. It launched a Future Industrialists initiative and a Voice of Industrialists platform, and it carried announcements on industrial complexes in Jubail and Dammam, an industrial master's degree and a furniture manufacturing diploma. A forum convened by the chambers of commerce rather than by a commercial exhibition organiser tends to produce institutional commitments of that kind — training programmes, platforms, memoranda between government bodies, universities and industry — rather than equipment orders.

The Jeddah location matters to what gets discussed. The western region's industrial base differs from the Eastern Province's hydrocarbon-anchored complex and from Riyadh's: it is weighted toward food processing, consumer goods, pharmaceuticals and the port-facing logistics that Jeddah Islamic Port supports. Several of the nine declared axes — food and pharmaceutical, perfumes and cosmetics, logistics — map directly onto that profile.

One observation is unavoidable four days out. Despite the claim of more than 80 speakers, the organiser has published no speaker names, no session titles and no timed agenda, and no exhibitor list or sponsor roster beyond the ministry partnership. For an event promoted extensively through the Saudi press on the strength of its patronage and its targets, the absence of programme disclosure at this stage is itself notable. Arab News has reported that agreements and memoranda between government, private sector, universities and research centres are anticipated, but that is forward-looking and unattributed to specific parties.
author: Mo Qureshi
companies: Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources
